title: Animate clip scale in OpenShot using automatic keyframes
note: In OpenShot 4.1, position the playhead on a clip and change a value such as scale in Properties while Auto Keyframes is enabled. Move to another time and set a new value. OpenShot interpolates between the recorded property values; the selected property's display reflects whether the current playhead is on a keyframe.

title: Choose OpenShot keyframe interpolation
note: OpenShot 4.1 supports Bézier, Linear and Constant interpolation modes for animated properties. Change the curve type from the graph control next to a property. Bézier eases movement, Linear changes steadily, and Constant holds one value until the next keyframe.

title: Apply OpenShot video or audio effects to clips
note: In OpenShot 4.1, drag an effect from the Effects tab onto a timeline clip. The effect is represented by a small icon; select it to show its parameters in Properties. Multiple effects can be combined, and supported parameters may be animated with keyframes.

title: Limit OpenShot effects to a mask or tracked area
note: OpenShot 4.1 allows effects to use a static or animated mask so they affect only part of the frame. Add an effect, open its Properties and choose a Mask Source; adjust Mask Mode to restrict the effect or change its strength. A Tracker can supply a moving masked region.

title: Create a visual crossfade in OpenShot
note: Overlapping two clips in OpenShot can automatically create a visual transition, represented as a blue rectangle. You can also drag a transition from the Transitions tab. These transitions affect video rather than audio; fade the clip's volume separately if an audio crossfade is needed.

title: Export an OpenShot project as an MP4 video
note: Select File > Export Video or the Export Video icon in OpenShot. The default output is an MP4 using H.264 video and AAC audio. Choose the project-matching video profile and adjust quality; the Advanced tab exposes encoding options when required.
